title: Distributed job orchestration
subtitle: One function definition runs as a job or a service, batched by rows or by GPU token budget, anywhere from in-process to rented cloud GPUs, by configuration.

stats.label: function crates built on the framework, beside eight service crates
control actions reaching running conductors, among them pause, scale, drain and inspect
probes in flight at the peak, never below 670K, from one decoupled producer over a two-hour capture

lede: I was going to build many systems and did not want to solve orchestration more than once, so I made FAFO Core and Function Forge one execution model that every function runs under. A function implements one Rust trait, and a generic conductor runs it along three independent axes over Redis and PostgreSQL. Services trigger continuously, on queue depth or on an interval. In submit-and-exit, a producer hands generation to the GPU broker and moves on while a completion service closes the loop; I split completion out after an embedded design made producers wait on results.
quote: Orthogonal axes over named modes: a new combination is a configuration change.
evidence: Distributed job orchestration: one Rust trait run as a job or a service, batched by rows or GPU token budget, in-process to rented cloud GPUs, under 13 function crates.
Control-plane design: 19 control actions, among them pause, scale, drain and inspect, reaching active conductors through a separate high-priority stream.
High-throughput batch inference: a decoupled producer holding 670K-970K probes in flight over a two-hour capture across Blackwell GPU hosts.
author: Corey James
